text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.47% today to $372.11, continuing a sharp five-day decline of roughly 10% from its peak at $412.85 last week. The drop aligns with a sharp deterioration in refining economics: while U.S. oil is trading at $89.53 per barrel, gasoline and diesel in storage are at elevated levels (215.9 million and 104.9 million barrels respectively), and refineries are running near capacity at 95.7%. This combination—ample product supply relative to demand—narrows the profit margin refiners earn by buying crude and selling finished fuel, a dynamic that has weighed on the stock consistently this week.

The broader backdrop is concerning for energy demand. Geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have created uncertainty about supply reliability, while record diesel prices in the U.K. and other regions suggest demand weakness relative to supply; refiners benefit from strong demand, not from rationed consumption. The stock's steep slide reflects the market repricing refining profitability downward in an environment of adequate supply and softening real-world demand signals.
